answer.rationale: Rollback is explicitly barred by compliance despite its historical success (b1), so that path is excluded regardless of memory strength. The write-path latency climb coincides with a genuine peak-traffic period, closely matching the pattern in memory_b3 where provisioning headroom before a retail peak absorbed surge and kept queue depth flat—this is the most directly analogous precedent for sustaining writes under load. Regional failover (b2) is tempting for fast latency recovery, but failovers carry real risk of dropping or duplicating in-flight writes during a settlement peak, which conflicts with the objective of not losing customer writes; I want the archived record on b2 to check whether write-safety during failover was actually validated or merely inferred. I also want to re-verify b3's archived record to confirm the capacity action was write-path capacity (not just read/dashboard offload) before committing capacity as the single available intervention this window. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing are better suited to dependency failure or read-load problems, not a generalized write-path latency climb under peak write volume, so they're deprioritized. I'm flagging downstream risk because capacity addition assumes the bottleneck is resource headroom rather than a lock/contention or replication issue introduced by the new release, which the current evidence doesn't rule out.
